pullQuote.title: As good as it looks
pullQuote.quote: First mallet I've owned and I love it. Great feel, great touch. Looks amazing, people definitely notice and my longer putts outside of 5 feet have gotten better.

buyBody: The putter you use more than any other club, and think about least. One hundred per cent CNC-milled from 304 stainless, with a slight toe hang that works with a natural arc instead of fighting it, and perimeter weighting that holds the line on strikes you miss. Right or left hand.

four.v: Plumber neck, for a natural arc

whatYouGet: One Tracer LGP02 Mallet putter in the hand you picked
Oversized 3.0 white and gold Lucky putter grip, fitted
Head cover: Confirm — several reviewers expected one and it did not arrive
carePara: The gold is a finish, not a coating that needs babying, but the face still wants wiping after a wet round so the ball comes off it the same way every time.
The grip is white. Reviewers have flagged that it picks up dirt quickly — a wipe with a damp cloth after a round keeps it looking new for a lot longer than it otherwise would.
marquee: Sold direct, never through a middleman
clubHeadline: The club you use twice as often as any other, and think about half as much.
clubParas: Nobody buys a putter for the reason they should. A driver gets picked over three weekends and a putter gets whatever was in the bag when you started. It is the club you use on every hole, twice, and it decides more of your score than anything else you carry.

The head is perimeter-weighted, so the strikes you miss off the toe hold their line instead of leaking away. The neck gives it a slight toe hang, which means it works with a natural arc in the stroke rather than asking you to putt straighter than you do.

It comes with the oversized 3.0 grip fitted, which is not a small detail. A fat grip takes the wrists out of the stroke, and the wrists are what turn a four-footer into a five-footer coming back. Reviewers mention it more than anything else on the club.
It costs $229 because we sell it to you directly and we don’t pay anyone on tour to play it — there is more on the pricing if you want it.

helpPick.headline: Both suit an arc. The question is feel or forgiveness.
helpPick.sub: This is the only question worth asking about a putter and the usual answer — mallets for straight strokes, blades for arcs — does not apply here. Both Tracers are built for a stroke with a natural arc. What separates them is how much the head helps you on the ones you miss, and how much it tells you about them.

options.name: Tracer Mallet
options.body: Slight toe hang from a plumber neck, so it works with the arc you already have. Perimeter weighting keeps an off-centre strike on line — you give up some feedback to get that.

options.name: Tracer Blade
options.body: For players who release the head through the stroke. Twenty grams heavier and far less forgiving, which is the trade — a blade tells you exactly where on the face you hit it.

helpPick.note: The blade is out of stock and right hand only when it returns. If you want the feedback rather than the forgiveness, that is worth waiting for.

specTabs.aside: Length is 35" and there is only one. Reviewers at 6′4″ and 6′7″ disagree about whether that is right for them, which is a real answer either way — a taller golfer should know before ordering that there is no long option yet.

look.photo: Bold, full-bleed, portrait. The putter head on the green at address, low sun raking across the gold and the white grip, the ball and the hole in soft focus beyond. Shot from the golfer's eyeline so the alignment reads.
look.headline: It gets noticed on every green you walk onto
paras: Putters are the one club everyone in the group sees you use, eighteen times a round, standing still, from four feet away. Most of them are grey. This one is gold and white, and the reviews are close to unanimous about what happens next.

That isn't the reason to buy it — the stroke is. But of every club in the bag, this is the one where looking down at something you actually like is worth the most, because you are looking down at it more than anything else you own.
look.aside: Everyone else is carrying the same putter with someone else's name on it. It's better to be lucky.

quote.q: Putter is well balanced and the weight is perfect. I switched from a blade style and it took a few rounds to get comfortable. Now I have the feel at all distances.

closeBody: The Tracer Mallet is $229, right hand or left, with the oversized grip already on it. Sixty days to send it back if it isn't the one.

bag.name: Tracer Blade
bag.hook: The arcing stroke's putter. More feel, less forgiveness, and currently sold out.

bag.name: Carver
bag.hook: The wedge most people add first. Six lofts, and they all feel like the same club.

bag.name: Stryker
bag.hook: Titanium hybrid at 19°. For the long approach the irons don't quite cover.
